title: Prove production share before optimizing a fast local helper

source.title: Representative structured-output ABBA on RTX 4060
source.claim_scope: One representative decode showed a 1.25x local mapping speedup but only 0.0385% baseline latency share and no measurable end-to-end gain.

implementation_recipe: Measure the target component self-time inside the frozen representative workload before implementing the optimization.
Compute its baseline latency share and an optimistic component speedup ceiling using an explicit removable-work argument.
Convert those values to an Amdahl end-to-end speedup ceiling and compare it with the frozen materiality floor.
Close or defer the opportunity when the optimistic ceiling is immaterial, even if an isolated microbenchmark is fast.
validation_recipe: Run baseline and candidate in an interleaved order and verify identical output hashes.
Record component call count, component self-time, total wall time and workload throughput in the same run.
Report the deletion upper bound as well as the observed component speedup.
Treat end-to-end changes smaller than run-order and thermal variance as no measurable gain.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Rejecting an immaterial helper redirects budget toward kernels or orchestration stages with larger production shares.
A locally removed cost may expose no visible bottleneck shift because launch, model compute or scheduling noise dominates it.
failure_modes: A microbenchmark denominator omits the model, scheduler, launch and synchronization costs that dominate production latency.
Inclusive profiler time double-counts child work and exaggerates the component contribution.
A synthetic batch shape is treated as representative without a frozen workload distribution.
An observed end-to-end fluctuation is attributed to a microsecond-scale change despite a much smaller Amdahl upper bound.
scope_limits: The RTX 4060 result rejects this specific structured-mapping opportunity for the measured decode workload, not all host-side optimizations.
A different workload may raise the component share and must be measured under its own frozen contract.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: End-to-end latency contains the target component plus unaffected work under the frozen workload.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: target component self-time versus all unaffected end-to-end latency
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Use Amdahl's law to combine the improved component with unchanged residual latency.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Admit only opportunities whose recomputed optimistic end-to-end ceiling clears the frozen materiality floor.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: One representative attribution run plus constant-time bound calculation per opportunity.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: The gate completes before candidate implementation and prevents downstream search fan-out.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: No extra production communication is introduced; the gate consumes existing trace and timing evidence.
invariants: component time does not exceed end-to-end time
declared global ceiling matches Amdahl's law
gain ceiling does not exceed removable component work
evidence is hash-bound to the frozen run
anti_patterns: infer production share from code complexity
keep optimizing below the materiality floor
claim a global gain from an isolated helper benchmark

candidate_archetypes.name: representative attribution before implementation
candidate_archetypes.template: Measure component share in the target workload, derive the optimistic Amdahl ceiling, and admit implementation only when it clears the frozen materiality threshold.
